description: Retrieval-quality fixtures for the semantic-search backend benchmark. Each query has a human-defined gold target (the file a developer would consider the correct answer), chosen independently of what any backend returns so the benchmark is not circular. A query counts as a hit when ANY expectedPath appears in the backend's top-k results. Keep queries phrased as natural-language concepts (not bare symbol names) so they exercise the semantic ranker rather than exact-name matching.

queries.query: coalesce overlapping semantic index updates into a single in-flight run plus one trailing run
cap the number of worker threads so background indexing does not pin every CPU core
register and build the semantic index when a workspace is opened
format semantic search hits for display including line ranges and scores
parse ripgrep JSON output including match and surrounding context lines
probe which indexed grep backend is installed and fall back to ripgrep
verify a downloaded binary against a SHA-256 checksum before making it executable
download a release archive and extract the binary out of the tarball or zip
decide whether GitHub read-only tools should be exposed by checking gh auth status
convert an absolute filesystem path into a path relative to the workspace root
classify a search query as either a regex pattern or a conceptual semantic question
resolve the path to the bundled semantic search binary shipped with the app
run an external command with a timeout and a lowered process priority
the agent tool that searches the codebase by regex or by meaning and auto-selects the mode
look up the validation schema for a settings key
migrate legacy per-project conversation threads to the new layout
